references.text: The covenant between God and Abraham through circumcision is established as a sign – verse 13 repeats and reinforces this requirement.
Abraham immediately carries out the command from verse 13: he circumcises all who were born in his house or bought with money.
A slave bought with money must be circumcised, reflecting the same principle as in Abraham's covenant.
God promises not to break His covenant or change His word – an everlasting covenant, just as the covenant of circumcision is called an everlasting covenant.
Stephen refers to the covenant of circumcision that God gave Abraham as a sign of the everlasting covenant.
Paul explains that Abraham received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness he had by faith.
Paul discusses the meaning of circumcision in light of the gospel and the obligation it entails.
The verse describes the actual fulfillment of the command given in the source verse.
Combines the definition of the covenant (17:7) with its concrete scope and sign (17:13).
Contrast between the physical sign of the covenant (flesh) and the inner transformation (heart) that completes the covenant.
